connection_condition: transactions_1k.CardID resolves to exactly one customers.CustomerID: 902 cards across 517 customers, and no card is shared between two customers
description: A payment card is issued to and belongs to one customer; a card has no meaning independently of the customer who holds it.

connection_condition: yearmonth.CustomerID references customers.CustomerID; all 30566 distinct yearmonth customers resolve to a customers row
description: A monthly consumption record is a component of one customer's history and cannot exist without that customer.

connection_condition: transactions_1k.CustomerID references customers.CustomerID; all 1000 rows resolve
description: A transaction line is a purchase made by one customer and is meaningless without that customer.

connection_condition: transactions_1k.GasStationID references gasstations.GasStationID; all 1000 rows resolve, covering 437 distinct stations
description: A transaction line records a purchase made at exactly one station, so it is a component part of that station's activity.

connection_condition: transactions_1k.ProductID references products.ProductID; all 1000 rows resolve, covering 28 of the 591 catalogue products
description: A transaction line is a sale of exactly one product, and the line has no meaning without that product.

connection_condition: gasstations.ChainID groups stations; the 5716 stations fall into 233 chains, the largest holding 1462 stations and many holding one
description: A chain is a commercial grouping made up of stations; a station belongs to one chain.

connection_condition: average monthly consumption differs sharply by segment in a strict order: KAM 45243.63, LAM 17618.44, SME 3833.30. These averages mix CZK and EUR customers and are therefore not directly comparable in magnitude
description: The customer segment is strongly associated with the scale of monthly consumption. The database assigns no business meaning to the segment codes beyond this observed ordering.

connection_condition: fuel lines imply a per-unit price of 23.273 for CZK customers (n=800) against 0.918 for EUR customers (n=54), a ratio of about 25
description: Every paid amount is denominated in the currency of the customer who made the purchase, so amounts from customers of different currencies are not additive.

connection_condition: for the 517 customers present in both tables, the ratio of average Consumption to average monthly transaction spend is 18.17 for CZK customers (n=475) and 17.32 for EUR customers (n=42), so both tables share one per-customer currency basis
description: Monthly consumption is denominated in the customer's currency on the same monetary basis as transaction paid amounts.

connection_condition: CZK customers pay 23.271 per fuel unit at CZE stations (n=797) and 23.71 at SVK stations (n=3), while EUR customers pay 0.917 at CZE stations (n=2) and 0.918 at SVK stations (n=52)
description: The country of the station where a purchase is made does not determine the currency of the amount paid; the customer's currency does, so cross-border purchasing does not by itself change the monetary unit.

connection_condition: the implied unit price equals the same line's paid amount divided by its quantity; for fuel products this yields 23.273 for CZK customers and 0.918 for EUR customers
description: The per-unit price is derived by dividing a line's paid amount by its quantity, and is defined only where the quantity is greater than zero.

connection_condition: monthly consumption and sampled transaction spend for the same customers and month sit on the same per-customer scale, at a stable ratio of about 18 in both currencies. transactions_1k holds only 1000 sampled rows over four days and cannot reproduce the monthly totals
description: Monthly consumption and transaction paid amounts measure the same kind of customer spend at different grains: the monthly value is the coarser, complete measure and the transaction value is a finer sampled observation.
